item.title: China’s hospital ships project a different kind of naval power in Africa
item.description: When the Auspicious Ark entered Dakar, Senegal, on September 25, the scene looked closer to a public health mission than a naval deployment. Senegalese people and members of the Chinese community were waiting at the port as the vessel arrived for the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to Senegal. The Auspicious Ark is a PLA Navy vessel. That places the visit within a wider Chinese maritime presence in Africa, something more often associated with anti-piracy patrols, port calls,... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Abdul Malik al Houthi, el nuevo enemigo islamista de Occidente
item.description: Mohamed bin Salman, el Príncipe Heredero y hombre fuerte de Arabia Saudí, tiene pesadillas con él. Benjamin Netanyahu ha dicho que correrá la misma suerte que los abatidos líderes de Hamás, Yahya Sinwar, y de Hizbolá, Hasán Nasrala. Es Abdul Malik al Houthi, el líder del movimiento rebelde de Yemen, los hutíes, que desde hace más de diez años controlan la capital, Saná, y, cada vez más, el paso estratégico de Bab el Mandab, que une el Mar Rojo con el océano Índico.Abdul Malik al Houthi no estaba llamado a dirigir el movimiento político-militar de la minoría chií de Yemen. item.title: China and Africa boost law enforcement ties in crackdown on cross-border cybercrime
item.description: From online-gambling rings in eSwatini to SIM swapping in Kenya and cybercrime networks in Zambia, a wave of cross-border fraud is drawing African governments and China into closer security cooperation. China hosted East African security ministers and police chiefs in Lianyungang, Jiangsu province, on September 10 for talks on terrorism, kidnapping, online fraud and other cross-border threats. China’s public security minister, Wang Xiaohong, said Beijing would strengthen law-enforcement... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
